findings.rationale: Three independent tools agree. (1) client_updates: mean_cos about -0.56 (z about -7.5), i.e. the update points against the federation median, with an anomalous median norm ratio of about 3.1. (2) client_performance at round 20: local AUC 0.690 versus pooled 0.7995, ECE 0.082 (z +4.0), and CITL -0.081 (z -6.0), so observed prevalence (0.205) is far above predicted (0.124). The local model is poor on its own data, which points to corrupted labels rather than a clean client sending a bad update. (3) subgroup_outcomes: observed/expected ratio is high in both sex groups (1.72 for Sex=0, 1.57 for Sex=1), i.e. positives are over-recorded relative to what the features imply. The drift per-round CITL for NY is negative from round 3 onward. The mean cosine is negative across the whole run, so I put onset at round 1.

Three independent tools agree. (1) client_updates: mean_cos about -0.53 (z about -7.3), min_cos -0.88, median norm ratio about 2.9, i.e. the update runs against the federation median. (2) client_performance at round 20: local AUC 0.684 versus pooled 0.80, ECE 0.082 (z +4.1), CITL -0.067 (z -5.1), so observed prevalence (0.211) is far above predicted (0.144). (3) subgroup_outcomes: observed/expected ratio is high in both sex groups (1.50 for Sex=0, 1.37 for Sex=1). This is a label-quality signature (normal AUC would instead suggest prevalence shift). Onset set to round 1 because the mean cosine is negative across the run.

Same signature as NE and NY. (1) client_updates: mean_cos about -0.53 (z about -7.3), min_cos -0.81, median norm ratio about 2.2. (2) client_performance at round 20: local AUC 0.705 versus pooled 0.80, ECE 0.077 (z +3.5), CITL -0.075 (z -5.5), prevalence 0.230 versus predicted 0.156. (3) subgroup_outcomes: observed/expected ratio of 1.48 in Sex=1 (z_noise about 5.8). Local performance is poor, so this is not a clean client with a manipulated update (poisoning). Confidence is slightly lower because the subgroup signal is only in one group.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then followed up on the strongest leads with per-round drift for NC, NE, NY and SC. Three clients (NE, NY, SC) show a consistent label-noise signature across tools: updates pointing against the federation median (mean cos about -0.53 to -0.56), low local AUC (0.68 to 0.71) with CITL around -0.07 to -0.08, and observed outcome rates well above predicted in the subgroup screen. Their local performance is abnormal, so I classed them as label noise rather than poisoning. Other candidates were not reported: NC (GenHlth p99 z_noise -6.1, with no persistent drift or performance anomaly), ND (HighChol sd z_noise 5.9, with normal performance), and several small-client drift onsets and feature outliers (DC, GU, VI, NV, SD, NH) that were within noise, with normal local AUC/CITL. The budget is fully spent (0 left). The NC and ND items are unresolved and could be checked with more budget if needed.
